failures.title: Bentley W12MULLINER Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cooling System Leaks - Expansion Tank, Plastic Fittings, Water Pump
items.whatHappens: The W12MULLINER runs extremely hot - all that power concentrated in a compact W12 package generates serious heat. Plastic coolant fittings become brittle, expansion tanks develop hairline cracks, and water pumps wear. A sweet smell from the engine bay or a small puddle in the garage are the tell‑tale signs. Ignoring coolant leaks leads to overheating, and overheating can cause serious engine damage. The W12 is known to be incredibly robust - one documented example withstood potentially years of overheating and still ran smoothly - but it is not invincible.
items.repairVsReplace: Catching a coolant leak early is straightforward and relatively affordable. Ignoring it leads to overheating, and overheating leads to very expensive problems. If caught before overheating, replacement of the affected components (expansion tank, fittings, water pump) is viable. If the engine has been severely overheated, a full rebuild or replacement may be required.

items.title: 48 Spark Plugs and 12 Ignition Coils - Ignition System Wear
items.whatHappens: The W12MULLINER has 12 cylinders, 12 ignition coils, and - critically - 48 spark plugs. Four per cylinder. By 50,000 miles, original spark plugs are due for replacement; coils often follow. Symptoms include subtle misfires, slightly rough idle, or a check engine light that comes and goes. Common diagnostic trouble codes include P032700 (Knock sensor 2 Circuit Low input) and P033200 (Knock sensor 1 Circuit Low input).
items.repairVsReplace: This is routine maintenance, not a reason to replace the engine. However, the 48‑plug count makes it an expensive service item - factor this into ownership costs.

items.title: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover Gaskets and Camshaft Position Sensors
items.whatHappens: Bentley W12 engines can develop oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and camshaft position sensors. Such leaks can result in poor oil pressure and eventual engine damage if not handled in time.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket and seal replacement is labour‑intensive but not engine‑replacement territory. Ignoring oil leaks that lead to low oil pressure can destroy the engine.

items.title: Vacuum System Leaks and MAF Sensor Contamination
items.whatHappens: Vacuum system leaks from aged hoses or plastic components, along with MAF sensor contamination, can cause various performance issues and trigger "Check Engine" lights.
items.repairVsReplace: Hose and component replacement is the standard fix. Not engine‑replacement territory unless ignored and causing further damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: The W12 engine itself - when properly maintained - is what owners on enthusiast forums call "bomb proof". Bentley overengineered the fundamentals - block, heads, internals. Mulliner‑spec engines benefit from the most rigorous testing regime: each W12 engine passes through three specific test regimes including leakage testing, cold testing (measuring 600 individual properties), and a 15‑minute cycle at 120 RPM to identify even the briefest anomalies. The engine has been retired after two decades and over 100,000 examples built.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the W12MULLINER
variants.intro: The W12MULLINER is the most exclusive iteration of Bentley's 6.0‑litre W12, reserved for Mulliner‑specification and coachbuilt models. It is hand‑built over 6.5 hours by a team of 45 craftspeople at Bentley's Crewe factory and is distinguished by unique engine management calibration, bespoke ancillaries and, in some cases, upgraded internals. The engine code is stamped on the engine block - typically on a machined pad near the front or side of the engine. It also appears on the V5C registration document and can be retrieved via Bentley's VIN decoder. Key variants: - Continental GT Mulliner W12 (2022-2024): 659 PS (650 bhp), 900 Nm (664 lb‑ft). 0‑60 mph in 3.5 seconds, top speed 208 mph. - Flying Spur Mulliner W12 (2022-2024): 626 bhp, 900 Nm (664 lb‑ft). 0‑60 mph in 3.7 seconds, top speed 207 mph. - Bacalar (2020-2021): 659 PS (650 bhp), 900 Nm (667 lb‑ft). Limited to 12 units. - Batur (2022-2024): 740 bhp, 737 lb‑ft (1,000 Nm). Limited to 18 units - the most powerful W12 ever. - Batur Convertible (2024): 750 PS (740 bhp). Limited to 16 units - the most powerful W12‑engined Bentley ever. Why fitting the wrong variant matters: The W12MULLINER has multiple variants with significantly different power outputs, ECU calibrations, turbocharger specifications and, in the case of the Batur, unique internals. A Continental GT Mulliner engine is not a direct swap for a Batur unit - engine mounts, wiring looms, cooling systems and transmission compatibility all differ. The Batur's 740 bhp engine uses upgraded internals that are not present in standard Mulliner units.

relatives.description: - the Speed-tuned 6.0-litre W12 that preceded the Mulliner variant. The W12MULLINER builds on the Speed's enhanced calibration with even more power, bespoke engine management, and in the case of the Batur, unique upgraded internals.

the 4.0-litre V8 PHEV producing 771 hp that replaced the W12 in 2024. This hybrid powertrain marks the end of the W12 era at Bentley, though future Mulliner models may receive bespoke hybrid calibrations.

relatives.code: The W12MULLINER is exclusive to Bentley's Mulliner division. Unlike the earlier W12, the Mulliner-tuned versions were never offered in Volkswagen or Audi models. The engine is hand-built at Crewe and represents the pinnacle of Bentley's 12-cylinder engineering. Over 100,000 W12 engines have been handbuilt at Crewe since 2002.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement W12MULLINER - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used W12MULLINER is an exceptionally rare proposition - fewer than 1,000 Mulliner‑spec W12‑powered Bentleys exist worldwide. If you do find one, cooling system history and service records are everything - a W12MULLINER that has been overheated is a major gamble. Only buy a used unit with documented full service history and, ideally, proof of the engine's hand‑assembly test records. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper W12MULLINER recon addresses the cooling system as a priority (new expansion tank, water pump, all plastic fittings), replaces all gaskets and seals (valve covers, oil cooler), inspects and refurbishes the twin turbochargers, performs a full carbon clean, and replaces all 48 spark plugs and 12 ignition coils. Given the rarity and value of these engines, reconditioning should only be entrusted to specialists with Bentley W12 experience. The 12-24 month warranty is essential given the complexity. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for the ultra‑rare coachbuilt models (Bacalar, Batur, Batur Convertible) or where the original engine has matching‑numbers value. An upgraded rebuild should include new timing chain components, upgraded turbocharger cores, forged pistons and a full bottom‑end refresh. For Batur‑spec engines, the unique 740 bhp internals must be replicated exactly. The W12MULLINER is not a DIY proposition - only a specialist with Bentley W12 and Mulliner experience should undertake this work. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted UK Bentley specialists can supply and fit your W12MULLINER - nationwide delivery, 12‑month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units, and fitting typically completed within 3-6 weeks given the complexity and rarity of these engines. View supply and fit VEHICLE VALUE NOTE (mandatory): The W12MULLINER sits in vehicles worth £200,000-£2,000,000+ (Bacalar and Batur models start at £1.5m-£2m). With a reconditioned unit at £18,000-£32,000+ plus fitting, the total cost represents a small fraction of the vehicle's value for coachbuilt models. For lower‑value Continental GT Mulliner examples (£150,000-£250,000), replacement remains justifiable. However, given the extreme rarity of these engines, sourcing a replacement is the primary challenge - not the cost. Always get a professional inspection before committing to any replacement.

items.question: What are the most common problems with the Bentley W12MULLINER engine?
items.answer: The most common issues are cooling system leaks (expansion tank, plastic fittings, water pump) which can lead to overheating, and ignition system wear (48 spark plugs and 12 coils needing replacement by 50,000 miles). Oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and camshaft position sensors are also reported, along with vacuum system leaks and MAF sensor contamination. The W12 is "bomb proof" when properly maintained, the cooling system must be inspected annually to prevent overheating, and diagnostic trouble codes P032700 and P033200 are common on W12 engines.

items.question: Should I buy a used, reconditioned or rebuilt W12MULLINER?
items.answer: Used W12MULLINER units are exceptionally rare - fewer than 1,000 examples exist worldwide. Reconditioned units (£18,000-£32,000+) are the best option for most owners - they address cooling, turbos, carbon and all gaskets. Rebuilt units (£25,000-£45,000+) are for the ultra-rare coachbuilt models (Bacalar, Batur, Batur Convertible) where matching numbers are essential. A new OEM unit (£65,000+) is only sensible for cars under warranty, a 12-24 month warranty is essential given the rarity and complexity, and fitting costs are significant; factor them into the total.

items.answer: The engine code appears on the block and V5C. The W12MULLINER is distinguished by its Mulliner-specific calibration and, in the case of the Batur, unique upgraded internals. Key identifiers: the vehicle will be a Mulliner‑specification or coachbuilt model, and the engine management calibration is unique to Mulliner applications. items.question: How reliable is the Bentley W12MULLINER engine compared to the base W12?
items.answer: The W12MULLINER is considered as robust as the base W12 when properly maintained. Bentley overengineered the fundamentals - block, heads, internals. Mulliner-spec engines benefit from the most rigorous testing regime: each W12 engine passes through three specific test regimes including leakage testing, cold testing (measuring 600 individual properties), and a 15‑minute cycle at 120 RPM to identify even the briefest anomalies. Regular oil changes (every 6,000-8,000 miles) are critical, the cooling system must be inspected annually, and the W12MULLINER can exceed 150,000 miles with proper care.
